sources.citation: Weimer, Harry & Natalia Weimer. 1977. Phoneme comparisons of the Yareban family. Ms., SIL Ukarumpa (Technical Studies Dept.), 18 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 31250.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The only phonological description that covers Aga Bereho (=Bariji): vowels, consonants (13 in Aga Bereho, f~h), contrastive pairs. No suprasegmental/stress section and no stress rule for any Yareban language (the only prose on stress, p.5, concerns the Oiso dialect of Maria). The 140-item wordlist pp.6-11 marks stress with an acute on every Aga Bereho form, e.g. kohíri 'head', óhe 'skin', ího 'knee', amára 'man', áinibinu 'he lies down', totóru 'path', wáka 'stone', ísu 'stick', sakáí 'earth', dubáwaru 'black', yáhawere 'long', húwiatu 'short' -- stress on 1st or 2nd stem syllable, not predic…
